# 60-second pitch

*Generated by `presentation/build.py` from `artifacts/*.json`. Numbers update when the experiments are re-run.*

**[0:00]** Time crystals are the most robust phase a driven quantum chain can have. Robust sounds like a good memory. So: is a time crystal a better quantum reservoir computer?

**[0:10]** We built one: six spins, a disordered kicked Ising chain. Each step we reset one qubit to encode the input, kick the chain twice and read out 11 expectation values. Only a linear readout is trained. Everything is exact density-matrix simulation, checked against Qiskit Aer.

**[0:22]** First answer: no. Time-crystal order freezes the spins. Memory capacity is 1.32 in the time crystal and 5.75 in the scrambling regime, about what an 11-node echo-state network gets.

**[0:32]** Second: real data, fair fight. Sunspots and CO2, same features, same splits, tuned on validation only, 8 seeds. Linear AR wins both. The ESN is second. The quantum reservoir is third: on CO2 it is far better than its no-interaction control; on the main sunspot split it only matches persistence. And it is not one lucky split: across 4 rolling-origin folds the top three keep that order.

**[0:47]** Third: hardware. With 1,000 shots per readout its memory drops to 2.64, and every readout means re-running the sequence.

**[0:55]** No quantum advantage. What we offer is an honest, reusable benchmark, and a replication of Zhang et al. 2025 on real data. Thank you.
